V-M-PORTABLE-EXPORT.Scenario: Export preserves source files and visible content, uses explicit file and anchor destinations, is repeatable and refuses to overwrite an unowned folder. The relocated package opens every page under file URLs and supports both-language search, language switches, theme carry-over, embedded fonts, diagram zoom and manual copying without external resource requests. Each section bundles its own search index; the neighbour browser check exercises cross-section navigation and Discovery search in a disposable export. Static mode protects independently portable EN/RU folders, no scripts or dead controls, fixed light rendering under a dark OS preference, complete authored reading text and workflow popup descriptions, native disclosures and stage fragment reveal, visible board sections, all Lab tasks, topic links, standalone diagrams, local fonts and responsive direct-file layouts. All static pages and local destinations are checked after relocation without sibling editions.

A local Chromium pass does not establish corporate Windows SMB access, browser policy or file associations. External references still need their usual access. The export only contains the last generated website state.
V-M-PORTABLE-EXPORT.TraceAssertion: Commands exit zero. Interactive evidence is in .runtime/portable/browser-report.json; static evidence is in .runtime/static-export/browser-report.json. Reports bind to the manifest/source tree and actual direct-file reading paths.

V-M-PORTAL-NEIGHBOURS.Scenario: Shared Kanban checks protect native card identity and production sample exclusion. A disposable nonempty Delivery consumer exercises actual rendered summaries, Waiting dependencies, selection replacement, keyboard activation, Close/Escape focus return, tab clearing, modified-click/no-script navigation and portable output; actual Portfolio checks cover filter-hidden clearing and Review/Standing selection. Computed card typography, spacing, radius, surfaces and contrast match between both consumers across EN/RU, four widths and both themes. Fixtures never modify maintained records or production output. Portfolio fixtures protect shared ordinary capacity, Waiting context and retained capacity, off-flow exits, standing exclusions, recorded order and unknown dates/measures. Current-record checks compare all eleven identities, board/register/search destinations, milestone projection and role-safe fields. Source disagreements and changed WIP limits are tested. Browser checks cover every summary and register/workflow route in EN/RU at four widths and two themes, priority/text filters, empty results, keyboard tabs, inline detail dismissal/focus return, search, counterpart routes, contrast, no-script reading and disposable direct-file output. Delivery fixtures verify ordinary continuation, Standing admission, explicit hierarchy, Completed versus acceptance, Waiting capacity, a nonempty maintained-record-to-card path and inconsistent counts. Actual baseline checks preserve an empty Program Backlog and one new Proposed INI-013 intake; browser checks exercise five columns, three service classes, all intake relationships, scoped filters/search, Portfolio/project round trips, both editions at four widths/two themes, keyboard tabs, no-script and portable paths. The generated site exposes the router with exactly the five branch doors and counted facts, five navigation groups, branch-local search with a global scope over every branch index (on by default only on the router), bounded relationship links, equivalent language routes, stable page references across renamed routes and separate statuses. Discovery retains every source page, scenario and context statement with unchanged source text and identifiers; the additional Regulatory Horizon pages retain their authored links and scenario marks. Shared card layouts cover overview, domain, detail and workflow pages without clipping. Chromium covers every branch page outside the Center, both routers and Center samples at desktop and mobile widths in both themes, the router doors and the brand link, global search on HTTP and direct-file output, keyboard-operated scenario disclosures, tabs, source stage dialogs, overview and domain stage links, keyboard focus, section switching, language counterparts and search fragments. AI Lab retains all source blocks, task/lane assignments and supplied coverage values, with identical unit keys in Russian and fail-closed translation freshness. Lab browser checks cover every stage/lane combination, reset, task search, fragment reveal, sidebar anchors, shared feedback, both themes, four viewport widths, scripting-disabled reading and direct-file controls. The service-resolution project retains all twelve source bodies, 64 tables and seven diagrams per edition, with independently compared text atoms and graph geometry. Browser checks cover every document and diagram in both languages/themes at desktop and mobile widths, smaller/intermediate views, section and intra-project references, search, counterpart routes, native modal zoom/fit/actual-size/pan/close/focus behavior, no-script reading and portable output. Center search, diagram zoom and template copying remain functional. A disposable file package resolves all pages and supports section-scoped search and navigation.

Portfolio checks do not authorize business cases or decisions, confirm achieved benefits or provide shared editing. Registry remains the maintained operational and evidence source. These checks do not validate the banking assumptions or illustrative measures in the retained Discovery material, establish project approval, validate AI Lab as approved Bank policy or its illustrative scorecard as measured readiness, or prove corporate SMB browser policy. Do not run the browser sweep while rebuilding the generated output.
V-M-PORTAL-NEIGHBOURS.TraceAssertion: All commands exit zero. Browser evidence is recorded in .runtime/kanban/browser-report.json, .runtime/delivery/browser-report.json, .runtime/portfolio/browser-report.json, .runtime/portal-neighbours/browser-report.json, .runtime/ai-lab/browser-report.json and .runtime/project/browser-report.json. The full-site link and repeat-build checks remain owned by V-M-PORTAL-SOURCE and V-M-PORTAL-PROJECTION.

V-M-PORTAL-SOURCE.Scenario: Pinned English source hashes match the language layout, reviewed translations match their source identities and revisions, the output holds exactly the gateway, the 404 page, the assets and per language the router and the five branches, every href, src and search index of every page resolves, every search result reaches its page and anchor inside its branch, and rebuilding the static site is repeatable.
Passing does not prove translated content exists or that the pages look right in a browser. Missing content translations are warnings only.
V-M-PORTAL-SOURCE.TraceAssertion: The command must exit 0. Its evidence covers the source and the projection consistency, not browser behaviour.

V-M-PORTAL-PROJECTION.Scenario: Both language route sets, in the router-and-branches layout with no former route, have resolved internal links, anchors, assets and search destinations. The actual renderer selects reviewed Russian text, source identity, search and diagrams, and renders missing translations as marked English.
Static checks and renderer fixtures do not prove screen-reader behavior, visual layout, or complete translation. The older first-slice browser script is not a current whole-site acceptance gate.
V-M-PORTAL-PROJECTION.TraceAssertion: Both commands exit zero. The page count, source-language attributes, counterpart links, and repeated build output are observable evidence.

V-M-AICC-DEPLOY.Scenario: Unit tests and integration tests pass: hashing vectors, folder diff, manifest, HTTP client, safety refusals, dry run writes nothing, publish mirrors and removes stale files and pushes origin then websvc, a second run does nothing, and verification compares the served manifest.

Passing does not prove the real server hook, Caddy, or Cloudflare path works. Integration tests use temporary repositories and local bare remotes, and never touch the real deploy repository. The first real publish is verified by the tool's own served-manifest check.
V-M-AICC-DEPLOY.TraceAssertion: Both commands must pass. Evidence covers the deploy tool only, not the portal build, which is verified by V-M-PORTAL-SOURCE.

V-M-PORTAL-LOCALIZATION.Scenario: Reviewed Russian source renders with its own language and translated identifier while retaining canonical record identity. Draft/missing translations keep English text and identity. Localized tables use stable canonical lookup keys.
Stale hashes, wrong document identifiers, changed numbered clauses, table-shape drift, changed record dates, and orphan translations are rejected.
V-M-PORTAL-LOCALIZATION.TraceAssertion: Tests and source checks exit zero. Human review still establishes semantic equivalence and professional terminology.
